### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ed0b4d348b51cc19f60d829181a5d7a57af1b7a` — the merge of head `5cb5e1b8e0f11aafb5937f68d4b322f9cbc5326d` into base `cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ed0b4d348b51cc19f60d829181a5d7a57af1b7a && git checkout 4ed0b4d348b51cc19f60d829181a5d7a57af1b7a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c 5cb5e1b8e0f11aafb5937f68d4b322f9cbc5326d && git checkout -B drift-repro cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c && git merge --no-ff 5cb5e1b8e0f11aafb5937f68d4b322f9cbc5326d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-publish-drafts-request-conformance.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-publish-drafts-change-note.integration.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`error()`, `handlePackages`), packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts (`buildApiError`), packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts (`readRequestBody`), packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (the twin body read), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` docblock, on `main`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`packages.publishDrafts`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts (`publishPackageDrafts`), .changeset/28452-publish-drafts-message-refused.md (on `main`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Face: the narrowing face alone. `reviewFace` over the five committed paths returns no `hits` (no published-schema source and no governed path; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success` on this head) and hands the decision to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm on both carriers, so the record is at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with the narrowing floor: every diff path outside the prose face. The one prose-face path, `.changeset/28541-publish-drafts-non-object-body-refused.md`, is read for ② below. PR #28593 is draft, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, three commits on `claude/project-thread-i4gkt8` over base `c658320792` plus a merge of `origin/main` at that same commit; five files, +88/−1. Read against card #28541 and its claim `6554240344`, the seat's order, the dev report `6554870967`, merged PR #28527 and its review `6553704063` (③ residual), and merged PR #28447. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the record template was printed from `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --face narrowing`, which reads no board.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change at `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts`, derived from the one code hunk in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (the `publish-drafts` branch, placed after the `404` and before #28527's `message` parse):

1. **What moves from accept to refuse: exactly the bodies that are present and are not a plain object.** The guard is `body !== undefined && body !== null && (typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body))`, and only a body it admits is handed to `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema.safeParse` as a whole; the schema is `z.object(...)` under zod 4, so every value the guard admits fails the parse. Moved from `200` (published, default note) to `400`: an array (`[]`, `['message']`), a string (`'x'`, `''`), a number (`42`, `0`), a boolean (`true`, `false`). The suite pins all eight. Judged correct and exactly the order's set, with booleans included (③ below).
2. **The boundary cases, each measured from the code.** `{}` stays `200` with no note (the accepted-bodies pin still carries it, the guard admits it and nothing in it is read). An absent body: in-process `undefined`, admitted; on the wire, `readRequestBody` answers `{}` for a request with no body and for an empty or whitespace-only `application/json` body (`if (text.trim() === '') return { body: {} }`), and the twin read in `packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts` does the same, so an absent or empty body never reaches the guard as anything but `{}` or `undefined`. JSON `null` reaches the handler as `null` (`JSON.parse('null')`), the guard admits it and the pre-existing pin "an absent body reads as `{}`" (`[undefined, null]`) still passes. An empty-string body as JSON (`""`) is a string and is refused; a raw empty body is `{}` and is not. A non-JSON media type with a body never reaches the door: the transport refuses it `400 INVALID_REQUEST` at the read, unchanged. Judged correct and consistent with the order's "keep an absent body, an empty body and a JSON `null` as no body".
3. **Envelope identity with the siblings; no second envelope.** The leg answers `deps.error(text, 400)` with no explicit code, exactly as the `message` leg beneath it and the install door's `manifest.id`, `manifest.version` and whole-body legs do; `HttpDispatcher.error()` hands it to `apiErrorResponse`, whose `buildApiError` derives the code as `input.code ?? promoted ?? standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(400)`, so `VALIDATION_ERROR` is derived and nothing in `packages/spec` moves. The headline is spelled the install door's way, the issue path or `(body)` for the root (`Invalid publish-drafts body — (body): Invalid input: expected object, received array`), and ends in the prescription (send a JSON object, or no body). Judged correct.
4. **Nothing is published and no history row is written on refusal.** The leg returns before `resolvePackageWriteActor`, before `protocol.publishPackageDrafts`, before the ADR-0045 re-save loop. Pinned at two layers: over a protocol double (`publishPackageDrafts` and `saveMetaItem` never called, eight bodies) and over the real protocol on on-disk SQLite (`[]`, `'x'`, `42`: no `publish` row in `sys_metadata_history`, no row in `sys_metadata_commit`, and the same pending draft then publishes with an object body carrying its note). Judged correct.
5. **Controls unchanged.** An object body never enters the new `if`, so `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema.safeParse` as a whole is never run on one: `backfill` keeps its one refusal (the protocol's, forwarded `...(body?.backfill !== undefined ? ...)` exactly as before; the real-protocol case with five malformed shapes and `publish` called once is unchanged and green), a non-string `message` keeps #28527's sentence (`message: Invalid input: expected string, received number`; the five-body pin is unchanged), `{ actor: 'x', message: 'note' }` still answers `200` with the caller recorded and `actor` reaches neither the publish nor the ADR-0045 re-save (both pins unchanged, #28414 untouched). The `403`, walled, closed-query, `501` and `404` legs precede the new leg and are untouched. Judged correct.
6. **The merge of `main` is clean and alters none of #28512's hunks.** `0ecc2c494` (PR #28512) is an ancestor of `c658320792`, the merge's second parent, which is also the merge-base with current `main`; `git diff c658320792 5cb5e1b8e` on `packages.ts` is the 26 inserted lines of this leg and nothing else, and on `route-ledger.ts` the one row-note line. The ADR-0146 D3 import, the `ensureCustomizationPackage` protocol member, the install door's pair refusal and the `ensure-customization` door arrive through the merge byte-identical to `main`. Judged correct.
7. **Pins and ledger.** `packages-publish-drafts-request-conformance.test.ts`: the header gains the whole-body sentence (present non-object refused with the schema's own issue; `undefined` and `null` a publish with no note) and a new case over the eight bodies asserting the schema refuses each, status, code, headline prefix `Invalid publish-drafts body — (body): `, and no producer call. `packages-publish-drafts-change-note.integration.test.ts`: the real-SQLite case above. `route-ledger.ts`: only the publish-drafts row's `note` string changes (a present non-object body is refused 400 with the schema's whole-body issue, an absent one publishes with no note); `requestSchema`, `responseSchema`, `disposition`, `client` and every other field are unchanged, so the client's ledger resolver and the ledger tests are unaffected. Judged correct.
8. **Public surface.** No export, type or `describe` text moves anywhere; `packages/spec` is not in the diff, so no `api-surface`, `authorable-surface`, `json-schema.manifest` or `declaration-map` shard is owed. The `.d.ts` bytes of `@objectstack/spec` are unchanged. Judged correct.
9. **First-party callers never send a non-object.** `packages/client/src/index.ts` `packages.publishDrafts` sends `JSON.stringify(opts ?? {})`, an object always; `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts` `publishPackageDrafts` sends an object literal built from `backfill` and `message` only, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every `ui/` call site reached (`StudioDesignSurface`, `PackagesPage`, `usePublishAllDrafts`, `PendingDraftsBar`, `AiChatPage`) goes through that method; `plugin-chatbot` reads the response (`publishHealth`) and fetches nothing itself; `packages/cli`, `skills/**` and `content/docs/**` contain no caller of this door. No first-party caller breaks.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct arm**, same spelling in the PR body and the changeset, arm closed before the em-dash reasoning so `readClause2Line` takes the arm: nothing is widened (no key, value or export added, no body previously refused is now accepted) and a body answered `200` is now refused. Matches the order and the claim.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`** is correct: the narrowing is on a REST request body, not on anything an author writes in metadata. Under `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis, `none` must grade every introduced entry `patch` and may move no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline: the one entry is `'@objectstack/runtime': patch` and no baseline is in the diff. Consistent.
- **Level and carriers.** `@objectstack/runtime: patch` only, which is right: `packages/spec` is untouched, so no `@objectstack/spec` line is owed (PR #28527 carried one because its docblock changed; this diff changes no spec file). The changeset carries `fix(runtime)!:`, the `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` banner and exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` admits when the body carries no FROM-to-TO consumer migration; the body carries none (nothing was ever stored for a refused body, and the one-line "send a JSON object, or no body" is the refusal's prescription to a caller, not a rewrite block). `check-empty-changeset.mjs`: non-empty frontmatter, and the diff adds its own changeset without editing the pending `28452-publish-drafts-message-refused.md` (a foreign changeset it may not touch); it instead names and supersedes that changeset's sentence "no body, or no `message`, publishes with the default note", the same device the #28527 review accepted for #28406's changeset. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. Judged consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 2, booleans refused.** The ruling says a present body "that is not a JSON object (an array, a string or a number)"; the parenthesis is a list of examples of the class, not the class, and `true` / `false` are present bodies that are not JSON objects by plain reading, which the schema refuses the same way. Refusing them is inside the ruling, not beyond it; leaving them at `200` would have kept a declared-not-enforced value on the same door. Accepted, and pinned.
- **Dev deviation 3, JSON `null` kept as "no body".** The order names a JSON `null` among the three shapes to keep as "no body", so this is the ruling applied, not a deviation. Measured from code: the transport hands it on as `null` (`JSON.parse('null')`), the guard's `body !== null` admits it, and the pre-existing pin treats `[undefined, null]` as absent. One residual is recorded for the seat, not as a must-fix: `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema.safeParse(null)` fails, so a JSON `null` body is the one declared-refused value the door still answers `200` on; it is by the seat's own ruling, the PR body states it plainly, and it is for the seat to carry or close (Prime Directive 10), not for this PR to widen.
- **Dev deviation 5, no spec docblock change.** The `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` docblock on `main` says the door reads exactly two body members and hands them to `publishPackageDrafts`, describes `message` (parsed with the member, refused `400` naming it) and `backfill` (judged by the protocol), says unknown keys are stripped, and says "the body is optional on the wire; an absent body reads as `{}`". Every sentence stays true on this head: the members are read as described for an object body, an absent body still reads as `{}`, and the body being a JSON object is what `z.object` itself declares. Nothing misdescribes the door; the docblock is silent on the whole-body refusal rather than wrong about it. Not touching `packages/spec` is correct (it would also have raised the schema face for a sentence nothing requires). No must-fix.
- **Dev deviation 1, red-first measured after the fix commit** by checking `packages.ts` out from `origin/main` under the new tests and restoring from `HEAD` (restore verified by an empty `git diff HEAD`). The measurement is the same measurement in a different order; accepted. **Deviation 4** (commit trailers reworded before push) is process, not contract.
- **`open_questions`: []**, **`out_of_scope_findings`: []** in the report. Accepted.
- **Evidence read in the dev report.** Red-first: both new cases red on the base door (`[]: expected 200 to be 400`), 13 controls green. Green at the fix: 23/23 across the two suites and the route-ledger tests. Ablation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the anchor `if (body !== undefined && body !== null && (typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body))) {` to `if (false && ...)`: anchor 1 to 0, blob changed, both new cases red, 13 controls green (string note, no body, `actor` stripped, undeclared members, non-string `message` refusal, real-protocol `backfill` refusal, `actor` on the re-save), restore blob equals head and `git diff HEAD` empty; the runtime tests import the door from `src/`, so no build sits between mutation and run. Transport probe (scratch, deleted): no body, no body as JSON, empty JSON body reach the handler as `{}`; `null` as `null`; `[]`, `"x"`, `42` as array, string, number; this matches `readRequestBody` as read above. Runtime typecheck exit 0; runtime suite 500 files, 8141 passed, 19 skipped; dogfood battery 363 files, 2932 passed, 28 skipped, no failure; 63 derived gate families run and reconciled with `--ran`. The ablation restores the exact prior behaviour and reds only the two new cases, so the evidence proves the mechanism, not the harness. Accepted.
- **Head check-runs at this read.** Completed `success`: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, the four `Type Check` lanes, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three scoped lint lanes, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`. Still `in_progress`: the eight `Test Core` shards and `Lint · docs & code guards`. This record is the contract-tier verdict; the landing pre-check that every check is green on this head is the seat's, read before the PR enters the queue.
- **Docs drift check** names `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` through `handlePackagesRequest`; that page's row 55b describes the walled-catalog refusal at the `/packages` write doors, which still precedes the new leg, so the page stays accurate. `skills/objectstack-platform/references/plugin-hooks.md` names the door only as the source of `metadata:reloaded`, unaffected.
- **Author.** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay author note is owed. The three branch commits carry no model identifier in title or body; none appears in the PR title, body, changeset or code comments.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Narrowing face, against the published spec on `main`.** The narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer: `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` on `main` is `z.object(...)`, so a caller that honoured the declaration never sent an array, a string, a number or a boolean as the body, and neither first-party caller can. What the diff does is make the declaration's own refusal real at the door (Prime Directive 12: refuse off-spec input at the producer-facing door), closing the declared-not-enforced remainder the #28527 review named under ③. The previous behaviour, publishing every pending draft of the package with the default note while the caller's body was silently ignored, is exactly the silent-tolerance class the four-axis framework's third axis forbids. Judged to hold.
- **The mechanism: a guard, then the schema as a whole, only for a non-object.** Parsing the whole body for every request would have made the door a second judge of `backfill` with a second sentence and no `issues[]`, displacing the protocol's one refusal, which the #28527 review already found to be the right thing to keep. Gating the whole-body parse on "not an object" means an object body never meets it, so both halves of the ruling hold at once: the schema's own sentence for the non-object class, one refusal for `backfill`, #28527's sentence for `message`. The refusal reuses the install door's issue-locating spelling (`path || '(body)'`) and the sibling envelope rather than a restated rule; the file's body-validating doors keep one pattern. The guard admitting `null` is a deliberate reading of the ruling, recorded under ③. Judged the correct trade.
- **Scenario the card is accepted against.** `[]` (and `"x"`, `42`) through the real door over the real protocol on SQLite: base `200` with the default note and a `publish` history row per draft; head `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with the whole-body issue, no history row, no commit row, the draft still pending, and the next object-body request publishes it with its note. Controls for every "unchanged" claim in the PR body (`{}`, no body, `null`, `{ message }`, `{ actor }`, bad `backfill`, non-string `message`) are pinned in the same suites and are green unchanged. The acceptance scenario holds.
- No must-fix found on the face.
